summary: The recorded base reproduces the timeout-path defect with no scheduler abort. The exact candidate sends an AbortReq before local rid cleanup and prevents the busy-scheduler health shortcut from swallowing that abort. Candidate regressions, existing abort cleanup tests, and an independent actual Scheduler.process_input_requests boundary test pass.

tests.what_was_measured: Failing-before timeout behavior: response was 503 but no scheduler abort was recorded; success control passed.
Candidate timeout abort ordering, success control, generation/embedding classification, ordinary request boundary, and health-prefixed AbortReq exclusion; 5 passed.
Focused candidate regressions plus broader tokenizer rid/abort cleanup behavior; 31 passed and 3 subtests passed.

tests.command: independent inline Python invocation of Scheduler.process_input_requests.__wrapped__ with a health-prefixed AbortReq and forced busy scheduler
tests.what_was_measured: The actual scheduler input path dispatched the abort, queued no health acknowledgment, and rejected AbortReq and non-tokenized lookalikes as probes.

gpu_execution.evidence: Control-plane Python cancellation behavior did not require a GPU kernel. Hardware inventory only: one AMD Instinct MI350X/gfx950, Torch 2.11.0+rocm7.2, HIP 7.2.26015.

remaining_limitations: The reported NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell architecture was unavailable; the assigned GPU was AMD Instinct MI350X/gfx950.
Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 weights and the reported NEXTN/262144-context serving configuration were unavailable.
The separate paged-prefill shape mismatch and NVIDIA driver reset were not reproduced or claimed fixed.
No full-model or multi-node reproduction was performed.
